name: Intuit

logo.source: commons.wikimedia.org (1920x408 px) - Wikipedia infobox logo file: Intuit-logo-super-blue (1).png

description: Intuit sells financial software to small businesses and consumers. Global Business Solutions (60 percent of revenue) is QuickBooks accounting, payroll, payments and Mailchimp marketing, sold mostly as online subscriptions plus payments and money-movement fees. The Consumer segment (40 percent) is TurboTax tax preparation, earned mostly in the US tax season January to April, Credit Karma, which is paid by lenders and card issuers for completed applications (cost-per-action), and ProTax software for accountants. The company is profitable at the segment level (77 percent and 73 percent margins before unallocated corporate costs) and returns cash by dividend and buyback.

gics.note: Conventional label as listed in the Wikipedia 'List of S&P 500 companies' table (GICS sector and GICS sub-industry columns). That table does not give the industry group or industry levels, so they are null rather than filled from memory.

employees.note: About 18,600 in seven countries, plus an average of about 12,300 seasonal employees January to April (FY2026 10-K)

businessLines.name: Global Business Solutions
businessLines.how: Monthly or annual QuickBooks subscriptions (tiered, with annual price increases and upgrades), plus per-transaction fees on payments and payroll, and subscription-based Mailchimp and desktop plans.
businessLines.description: QuickBooks Online, Intuit Enterprise Suite, QuickBooks Desktop, payroll (QuickBooks Workforce), payments, QuickBooks Checking, Mailchimp.

businessLines.name: Consumer
businessLines.how: TurboTax: a one-time fee per tax return (free to paid tiers, expert-assisted and full-service at higher prices), mostly January to April. Credit Karma: lenders and card issuers pay Intuit per qualified click or completed action, not the user. ProTax: annual software and e-file fees from accountants.
